chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim from Sulayman ibn Khalid who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who forgot to sit in the first two rak'ahs. He said: 'If he remembers before bowing, let him sit; and if he does not remember until he bows, let him complete the prayer. When he has finished, let him give the salam and perform the two prostrations of forgetfulness (sajdatay al-sahw).'
ai.seo_question: What should a Muslim do if they forget to sit for the first Tashahhud during prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the procedural distinction between correcting a missed sitting before entering ruku' versus performing the compensatory prostrations of forgetfulness (sajdat al-sahw) after completing the prayer. It reflects the Imami jurisprudence that prioritizes the continuity of the prayer structure, ensuring that minor omissions do not invalidate the act of worship but are rectified through specific, prescribed compensations.
